craft_notes: Sthāyin: chained-yet-officed; vyabhicāri exultation at divinity done small. Sanskrit-first: baddha (CHAINED — kept); pañcakṛtya (FIVE-ACTS — kept whole, standard Trika per UNC). Rows: 9 (making/keeping/loosing/veiling/blessing — five named, none trimmed; trimming would un-office the verse), 1 (‘blessing’ closes — anugraha last: grace ends the list). Close: ‘making, keeping, loosing, veiling, blessing’. Rupture: em-dash (chained stated, then its office). Rejected: trimming acts — killed: five are the office; ‘creating/preserving’ — killed: house verbs kept. Read aloud: CHAINED, yet IT-keeps THE-five-fold OFF-ice — … MAK-ing, KEEP-ing, LOOS-ing, VEIL-ing, BLESS-ing.

lines: Chained, yet it keeps the fivefold office —

reads_against.argmap: How does the bound one still act divinely? → Agency kept through contraction: likeness stained, five acts still done.
c1_essence: Stained likeness keeps divine office: five acts done small is wandering.
